messages.author: 8dd0defaec5cbad2
messages.subject: PARSER EXPECTED: <probability function argument> when appending transformed parameter to target
parts:
I get the error PARSER EXPECTED: <probability function argument> when I try to use transformed parameters to update the target in stan.  I'm trying to do this because I want Stan to output some log prior probabilities for robustness studies, though that use case won't be reflected in my simplified examples, which illustrate the problem but are kind of silly.  I am using stanc 2.12.0.

This gives the compiler error PARSER EXPECTED: <probability function argument>:
data {
    real x;
}
parameters {
    real mu;
}
transformed parameters {
    real mu_lpdf;
    mu_lpdf = normal_lpdf(mu | 0, 1);
}

model {
    target += mu_lpdf;
}

This works fine (and correctly stores the log probabilities in mu_lpdf):
data {
    real x;
}
parameters {
    real mu;
}
transformed parameters {
    real mu_lpdf;
    mu_lpdf = normal_lpdf(mu | 0, 1);
}

model {
    target += normal_lpdf(mu | 0, 1);

}


For what it's worth, the former also fails when I just set mu_lpdf = 2.0, so the problem seems to be with using transformed parameters in the target rather than with the normal_lpdf function.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PARSER EXPECTED: <probability function argument> when appending transformed parameter to target
parts:
Thanks. I can see where that's going wrong in the parser.
It thinks mu_lpdf is a user-defined probability function
because of the lpdf suffix, then fails to find its argument.
I can fix that. Here's the issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2123

We can probably get that in for the 2.13 release.

- Bob

           for (n in (m+1):D) {

                 Sigma_model_2[m,n] = 0;

                 Sigma_model_2[n,m] = 0;

   Omega_3 ~ lkj_corr(2.0); // regularize to unit correlation

     for (n in 1:N)  increment_log_prob( log(prior_pi[1]) + multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_1, Sigma_model_1), log(prior_pi[2]) + multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_2, Sigma_model_2), log(prior_pi[3]) + multi_student_t_log(trajectory[n], nu, mu_model_3, Sigma_model_3) );

> On Tuesday, January 3, 2017 at 10:03:30 PM UTC-5, Elaheh Torkashvand wrote:

>
> ERROR at line 81
>
>
>
> 79: Omega_3 ~ lkj_corr(2.0); // regularize to unit correlation
>
> 80: // Introducing no priors means we consider flat prior for the parameter. Note that the domain of the flat prior comes from the bound we have already defined for parameters.
>
> 81: for (n in 1:N) increment_log_prob( log(prior_pi[1]) + multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_1, Sigma_model_1), log(prior_pi[2]) + multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_2, Sigma_model_2), log(prior_pi[3]) + multi_student_t_log(trajectory[n], nu, mu_model_3, Sigma_model_3) );}

> Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name, :

You need to balance parens. I don't know what you were intending, but the
caret's pointing at the problem after the first multi_normal_lpdf --- what
did you expect commas to do, add? I'd suggest writing in a format
that makes that obvious and doesn't use such long lines
for (n in 1:N)
target += log(prior_pi[1])
+ multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_1, Sigma_model_1)
+ log(prior_pi[2])
+ multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model_2, Sigma_model_2)

+ log(prior_pi[3])
+ multi_student_t_log(trajectory[n], nu, mu_model_3, Sigma_model_3);

But my guess is that you wanted to implement a mixture model, in
which case you need t put those three components in (1, 2, and 3) into
a vector ps of size 3 and call

target += log_sum_exp(ps);

- Bob
